captions.detailed: This 3D model is a faucet-to-fountain adapter, designed to redirect water flow upwards. It features a main vertical body with a triangular cross-section and flat outer walls, which houses a circular inner channel to attach to a tap. Emerging from this body at a 45-degree angle is a hollow, triangular spout that directs the water upward, creating a drinking fountain stream. The bottom of the main body is cleanly truncated, leaving a flat base with a circular opening.
captions.instruction: Design a parametric faucet drinking fountain adapter in OpenSCAD. The model should consist of a vertical tube for the faucet attachment and an angled spout (fountain tube) branching off at 45 degrees, both with adjustable diameters, wall thicknesses, and heights. Ensure the bottom of the adapter is cut flat for easy printing.
captions.factory: The script constructs the adapter by performing a difference boolean operation on two main unions. The first union combines two low-resolution cylinders (representing the outer walls of the vertical tube and the 45-degree angled spout) with a specified Wall thickness. The second union contains two slightly longer, smaller-diameter cylinders to hollow out the inner flow channels. Finally, a translate and cube operation cuts off the bottom of the intersecting parts to create a flat, printable base.
